claim_being_audited: The actor claims the model can be certified for rollout because aggregate readiness passed and rollout controls exist, provided the certification record is conditioned on explicit model-card disclosure of the known enterprise refund workflow limitation.
specific_concerns: The actor's own summary says a named exposed segment remains below target and is still included in the initial rollout cohort.
The available policy text says rollout percentage, rollback, and monitoring do not remove disclosure duties when the affected segment remains exposed.
The risk acceptance draft is described as incomplete, unapproved, and not addressing the exposed enterprise refund workflow segment.
There is no admissible evidence in the record summary that the required model-card disclosure has actually been completed, reviewed, or attached to the certification action.
unsupported_claims: That certification is presently compliant on the available record, rather than only potentially compliant if required disclosure is completed before launch.
That rollout controls meaningfully cure the policy issue absent exclusion of the affected use case or approved risk acceptance.
Any implication that the disclosure condition has already been satisfied.
evidence_requests: Provide the final approved model card or disclosure text that explicitly documents the enterprise refund workflow limitation.
Provide evidence that the initial rollout cohort excludes the affected enterprise refund workflow segment, if that is being claimed.
Provide a reviewed and approved risk acceptance that specifically addresses continued exposure of the enterprise refund workflow segment.
Provide the final certification record showing whether certification is contingent on completed disclosure before launch.
decision_criteria: If the affected use case remains exposed, policy requires either explicit disclosure of the material limitation or approved risk acceptance covering that exposure.
Aggregate readiness and rehearsal results can support launch readiness, but they do not by themselves satisfy the disclosure predicate in the stated policy.
Certification is compliant only if the required support link is present in admissible evidence, not merely proposed in the actor's narrative.
